name: Old Swan House

location.state: Greater London (Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea)

dates.note: The list entry gives the single year 1876. The node's exemplar carries the year 1877 and its own note says 'Built 1875-77'. Neither is changed here.

refs.title: Swan House, Non Civil Parish - 1294208 | Historic England
refs.note: The Overview line carries Grade 'II*', List Entry Number '1294208' and Date first listed '24-Jun-1954'; the Details text prints '24.6.54' under the reference '63/14' and names the building 'No 17 (Swan House)'. The entry ends 'Listing NGR: TQ2762177720'. The register's name for the building is Swan House; the node's exemplar calls it Old Swan House, which is why `aka` carries both.

survey.prepared: Date first listed: 24-Jun-1954, as the Overview line prints it; the Details text prints '24.6.54'.

quotes.text: House. 1876. R Norman Shaw, architect. 4-storey, basement and dormers. Mostly 7 windows. Red brick tiled roof. Carved eaves cornice. Overhanging first and second floor, with second floor projecting beyond first floor, flanked by brick piers.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, opening paragraph (List Entry Number 1294208).

quotes.text: Three wide oriels with curved returns and semi-circular-headed central lights at first floor. Leaded panes. Second floor windows long and narrow with glazing bars, alternate windows 3-sided oriels with single brackets beneath. Central entrance with swan motif over door.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, openings paragraph, above 'Listing NGR: TQ2762177720'.

measurements.name: storey_count
measurements.note: Four storeys over a basement and under dormers; the fullest storey statement in this cluster and the only one from an urban terrace house.

measurements.name: front_window_count
measurements.note: 'Mostly' is the entry's own hedge: the front's window count varies by storey, which is exactly the effect the node's prose describes -- the elevation is composed storey by storey rather than on a single grid.

measurements.name: first_floor_oriel_count
measurements.note: At first floor. The node's own exemplar note says 'Three tall oriels on the first floor over a recessed ground storey', which the register corroborates for the count and does not corroborate for the recessed ground storey -- the entry says the first and second floors overhang.

note: Tranche 3, British picturesque and Arts and Crafts cluster, 5 Sep 2026. The most citable envelope statement in this cluster: a four-storey house over a basement, seven windows wide, with the first and second floors overhanging and the second projecting beyond the first. It is the one exemplar in these three nodes where the register states a storey count and a window-bay count for the same elevation in the same sentence.
